question: In round 2, when you rebuilt with Metal fastMathEnabled turned on and ran the 5-frame benchmark, what gpu_ms_best did it print?
answer:
gpu_ms_best = 100.887 ms.

How I know: that run's full output line is preserved in my archived history (message #133), from the 5-frame benchmark of the default scene at 512x512 / 64 spp, seed 1, --threads 8, after rebuilding with options.fastMathEnabled = YES (the build emitted only the macOS 15 deprecation warning for that property):

  render_ms_best=101.150 render_ms_avg=116.465 gpu_ms_best=100.887 spp=64 width=512 height=512 samples=16777216 threads_used=8

Context: the immediately preceding run without fastMath printed render_ms_best=101.771 (gpu_ms_best=101.237), so the difference was within the ~5 ms run-to-run noise on this machine — I logged fastMath as neutral and kept it enabled, noting the property is deprecated in favour of mathMode. For reference, the round-2 work later took the same scene down to gpu_ms_best=58.839 ms.

question: In round 2, when you rebuilt with Metal fastMathEnabled turned on and ran the 5-frame benchmark, what gpu_ms_best did it print?
answer:
gpu_ms_best = 100.887 ms.

How I know: the fastMathEnabled run was the 5-frame default-scene benchmark (512x512, 64 spp, seed 1, 8 host threads) right after I re-enabled `options.fastMathEnabled = YES` in src/pt_metal_host.mm (message #133). The program's printed line was:

  render_ms_best=101.150 render_ms_avg=116.465 gpu_ms_best=100.887 spp=64 width=512 height=512 samples=16777216 threads_used=8

For context, the run immediately before it (same median-split BVH, fastMath off) printed render_ms_best=101.771 / gpu_ms_best=101.237 (#129), so fastMath was effectively neutral (~0.3-0.6%, inside the ±5 ms noise on this machine); I left it enabled but it is deprecated in favour of mathMode. The big round-2 wins came later and elsewhere: near-first child ordering in the closest-hit traversal (93.5 -> 64.9 ms, #283) and kLeafSize 4 -> 1 (-> 59.1 ms best / 58.839 gpu_ms_best, #316).
